blocks.title: One reaction, alternative products
blocks.description: The process identity stays fixed. The result control changes only the product produced by this reaction.

steps.title: Substrate
steps.description: Define the substrate and reaction conditions.

steps.title: Product A
steps.description: Default product of this one reaction.

steps.title: Product B
steps.description: Alternative result of the same reaction under the stated conditions.

blocks.title: One pathogenic process, alternative results
blocks.description: The same host–pathogen process may resolve or progress; the control changes the result, not the pathway.

steps.title: Exposure
steps.description: Specify the pathogen and entry route.

steps.title: Host–pathogen interaction
steps.description: Define the shared process that can produce different results.

steps.title: Persistent tissue injury
steps.description: Default result when injury-producing mechanisms persist.

steps.title: Clearance and resolution
steps.description: Alternative result of the same host–pathogen process.

blocks.title: One drug mechanism, alternative results
blocks.description: The drug and target pathway remain fixed; the control changes only the resulting effect.

steps.title: Drug exposure
steps.description: Specify the drug and clinically relevant exposure context.

steps.title: Target engagement
steps.description: Specify one receptor, enzyme, transporter, or channel.

steps.title: Therapeutic result
steps.description: Default result produced through this drug–target mechanism.

steps.title: Adverse result
steps.description: Alternative result produced through the same drug–target mechanism.

blocks.prompt: Which choice best explains the mechanism?
blocks.answer: Explain why Choice B is correct and why the alternatives are less appropriate.
